textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · The Dairy Farm · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: When we multiply by 10, the number becomes 10 times bigger and each digit moves one place to the left. Multiplying by 100 shifts each digit two places left. So 3 x 100 = 300 and 20 x 50 = 1,000.

beats.en: When we multiply by 10, the number becomes 10 times bigger and each digit moves one place to the left. Multiplying by 100 shifts each digit two places left. So 3 x 100 = 300 and 20 x 50 = 1,000.
beats.speakEn: When we multiply by 10, the number becomes 10 times bigger and each digit moves one place to the left. Multiplying by 100 shifts each digit two places left. So 3 x 100  equals  300 and 20 x 50  equals  1,000.

beats.en: A shortcut: 30 x 20 = 3 x 10 x 2 x 10 = 6 x 100 = 600. Multiply the non-zero parts and then add the zeros.
beats.speakEn: A shortcut: 30 x 20  equals  3 x 10 x 2 x 10  equals  6 x 100  equals  600. Multiply the non-zero parts and then add the zeros.
